Project Statistics: • This project would replace the east grandstands at Meade Field. Project Statistics: • This maintains the track in the same general footprint reducing the costs and the need to displace any other fields or amenities within the existing athletic complex. This concept keeps the track in a north/south orientation but proposes to switch the common finish line to the northeast corner, which would allow athletes to finish most events with the prevailing winds at their backs. In the event winds change during a meet, the opposite finish line could be utilized based on the proposed layout. This concept proposes to remove several existing older buildings and a maintenance storage area close to the complex entrance off the northeast corner of the track. The removal of these buildings will ultimately create space for an ADA parking lot and a cleaner and more visually appealing entrance to the site. • $ 12,200,000 - RICAP • Status: Design Phase Kicked off in March 2024 • Start 2023 • Complete 2026 Kingston Campus - Locus Map Track & Field Replacement Ongoing Approved Project

Project Statistics: • In 2020 the University completed an advanced planning study for the replacement of the Tootell pools with a new natatorium building. Inclusive of converting the existing pools into an indoor playing field, this project had an expected price tag of $107MM assuming a 2027 completion. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Classification and Compensation Study Purpose of Submittal: Update the Committee on a recently launched classification and compensation study for URI’s non-classified staff.
Classified civil service positions, faculty, and graduate assistant positions will not be included as part of this review.
Points to Consider: URI is committed to fostering an inclusive, people -centered culture and continuing our efforts to attract, recognize, and retain outstanding staff and faculty.
In support of this strategic priority, we have recently launched a comprehensive review and revision of our classification and compensation structure for non- classified staff.
Huron Consulting Group was secured to support this study through a competitive Request for Proposal process.

Our goal is to develop a well -structured, transparent, and equitable compensation platform that provides clear pathways for advancement, rewards outstanding performance, and supports competitive compensation.
This modernization of our classification and compensation structure will result in a cohesive compensation philosophy, formal job architecture and career pathing, new job profiles more clearly connected to the competitive market, and policies and processes to sustain improvement.
The study is expected to take up to one year to complete.
Review and implementation of the study will be a multi- year effort, and we will work closely with the relevant staff and unions throughout the process.

President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval to exercise the options to purchase 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island and execute all documents relating to these acquisitions.
Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to exercise the options to purchase and execute all documents necessary for the acquisition of the properties located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: In April 1992, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the University of Rhode Island Foundation (the “Foundation”) with respect to land and buildings located at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, King ston, Rhode Island (the “Briar Lane Properties”) .

The Briar Lane Properties are currently the home of URI’s Police Department and its associated surface parking lot.
In May 2000, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the Foundation for land and buildings located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island (the “Plains Road Property”).
The Plains Road Property currently houses URI’s Fire and Life Safety and Environment Health and Safety offices.
The agreements grant the University options (the “Options”) to purchase the Briar Lane Properties and the Plains Road Property (together, the “Properties”) for $1.00 each upon fulfilling the University’s lease payment obligations.
It has been determined by the University and confirmed by the Foundation that those obligations have been met.
Recommendation: After a thorough review by and with all of the appropriate stakeholders, I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the request to authorize the exercise of the Options and direct that all required action be taken to consummate the acquisition of the Properties by the University.
Supporting Information: Please see attached Exercise Notices, Lease/Purchase Agreements from 1992 and 2000.

Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees hereby approves the request to exercise the University’s options to acquire title to the properties located at 177 Plains Road and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island, as granted to the University pursuant to the provisions of those Lease/Purchase Agreements related thereto and presented, and that the Board Chair, President and Vice President of Administration and Finance are each individually authorized, for and on behalf of the University and the Board of Trustees, to take all such actions and to execute all such documents as such person deems necessary and appropriate in furtherance of exercising such options and consummating the acquisition of the foregoing properties as recommended and presented.
